registers.name: OSCCON
registers.title: OSCILLATOR CONTROL REGISTER

fields.name: IDLEN
fields.text: Chooses what a SLEEP instruction does: enter Idle mode or Sleep mode.

fields.name: IRCF
fields.text: Picks the internal oscillator frequency; a change switches the clock frequency at once when the internal oscillator clocks the device. 111: HF-INTOSC, 16 MHz. 110: HF-INTOSC/2, 8 MHz (default). 101: HF-INTOSC/4, 4 MHz. 100: HF-INTOSC/8, 2 MHz. 011: HF-INTOSC/16, 1 MHz. With MFIOSEL (OSCCON2<0>) = 0: 010 HF-INTOSC/32, 500 kHz; 001 HF-INTOSC/64, 250 kHz; 000 LF-INTOSC, 31.25 kHz when INTSRC (OSCTUNE<7>) = 0, or HF-INTOSC/512, 31.25 kHz when INTSRC = 1. With MFIOSEL = 1: 010 MF-INTOSC, 500 kHz; 001 MF-INTOSC/2, 250 kHz; 000 LF-INTOSC, 31.25 kHz when INTSRC = 0, or MF-INTOSC/16, 31.25 kHz when INTSRC = 1. LF-INTOSC is the lowest-power internal choice.

fields.name: OSTS
fields.text: Shows whether the Oscillator Start-up Timer has run out and the primary oscillator is running; its Reset state follows the IESO Configuration bit (CONFIG1H<7>).

values.text: OST done; primary oscillator, set by FOSC<3:0>, running.
OST still counting; primary oscillator not ready, device runs on HF-, MF- or LF-INTOSC.

fields.name: HFIOFS
fields.text: Shows whether the HF-INTOSC frequency has settled.

fields.name: SCS
fields.text: Selects the system clock source; a change switches the clock source at once.

values.text: Internal oscillator block: HF-INTOSC, MF-INTOSC or LF-INTOSC.
Primary oscillator chosen by FOSC<3:0> (CONFIG1H<3:0>): OSC1/OSC2, or HF-INTOSC with or without the PLL.

fields.name: EEPGD
fields.text: Chooses whether an access goes to Flash program memory or to data EEPROM.

fields.name: WRERR

fields.name: WREN
fields.text: Permits or blocks write cycles to Flash program memory and data EEPROM.

fields.name: WR
fields.text: Starts a self-timed erase or write; software can only set it, and hardware clears it when the write is done.

values.text: Starts a data EEPROM erase/write, or a program memory erase or write; self-timed, cleared by hardware at completion, cannot be cleared by software.
The EEPROM write cycle has finished.

fields.name: RD
fields.text: Starts a one-cycle EEPROM read; software can only set it, hardware clears it, and it cannot be set while EEPGD = 1 or CFGS = 1.

values.text: Starts an EEPROM read, which takes one cycle; cleared by hardware, cannot be cleared by software, cannot be set when EEPGD = 1 or CFGS = 1.

fields.name: RXFUL
fields.text: Set by the CAN module when a message arrives; software clears it after reading the buffer. While it is set the buffer counts as full and no new message is loaded into it.

values.text: Buffer is free for a new message.

fields.name: TXBIF
fields.text: Transmit mode: set when the buffer has sent a message successfully. Cleared automatically when TXREQ is set.

fields.name: RXM1
fields.text: Receive mode: chooses which messages the buffer takes.

values.text: Every message, partial and invalid ones included; acceptance filters ignored.
Valid messages that pass the acceptance filters.

fields.name: TXABT
fields.text: Transmit mode: set when the message was aborted. Cleared automatically when TXREQ is set.

fields.name: RXRTRRO
fields.text: Receive mode, read-only: set when the received message is a remote transmission request.

fields.name: TXLARB
fields.text: Transmit mode: set when the message lost arbitration while it was being sent. Cleared automatically when TXREQ is set.

fields.name: FILHIT
fields.text: Receive mode: number of the acceptance filter that let the last message into this buffer.

fields.name: TXERR
fields.text: Transmit mode: set when a bus error happened while the message was being sent. Cleared automatically when TXREQ is set.

fields.name: TXREQ
fields.text: Set to ask for the buffer's message to be sent, which also clears TXABT, TXLARB and TXERR; hardware clears it once the message has gone. Clearing it in software while set asks for the message to be aborted. While it is set, or a transmission is under way, the transmit buffer registers are read-only.

values.text: Send requested; TXABT, TXLARB and TXERR cleared.
Cleared by hardware once the message is sent.

fields.name: RTREN
fields.text: Transmit mode: automatic answer to remote frames. When set, a received remote transmission request sets TXREQ by itself.

values.text: A received remote transmission request sets TXREQ.
A received remote transmission request leaves TXREQ alone.

fields.name: TXPRI
fields.text: Transmit priority: the order in which the transmit buffers are sent. The CAN message identifier is not changed.

fields.name: T3CKMX
fields.text: On 64-pin packages, picks the pin that clocks Timer3. Present only on PIC18F6XK80; keep at 0 on 28-, 40- and 44-pin devices.

fields.name: T0CKMX
fields.text: On 64-pin packages, picks the pin that clocks Timer0. Present only on PIC18F6XK80; keep at 0 on 28-, 40- and 44-pin devices.

fields.name: CANMX
fields.text: Picks which pins carry the ECAN CANTX and CANRX signals.

values.text: CANTX on RB2, CANRX on RB3.
CANTX on RC6 and CANRX on RC7 in 28-pin and 40/44-pin packages; on RE4 and RE5 in the 64-pin package.

registers.name: CONFIG4L
registers.title: CONFIGURATION REGISTER 4 LOW
notes: The register file summary gives the reset as 1--1---1.

fields.name: DEBUG#
fields.text: Turns the background debugger on or off; low turns it on.

values.text: Debugger off; RB6 and RB7 are general purpose I/O.
Debugger on; RB6 and RB7 serve In-Circuit Debug only.

fields.name: BBSIZ0
fields.text: Sets the size of the boot block.

fields.name: STVREN
fields.text: Sets whether a full or underflowed stack resets the device.

values.text: Stack full or underflow resets the device.
Stack full or underflow does not reset the device.

registers.name: DEVID2
registers.title: DEVICE ID REGISTER 2 FOR THE PIC18 F66 K80 FAMILY

fields.name: DEV
fields.text: Upper device ID bits, DEV<10:3>; with DEV<2:0> in DEVID1 they give the part number. These bits alone may match other devices; only all of DEV<10:0> names the device.

registers.name: DEVID1
registers.title: DEVICE ID REGISTER 1 FOR THE PIC18 F66 K80 FAMILY

fields.name: DEV
fields.text: Lower device ID bits, DEV<2:0>; read together with DEV<10:3> in DEVID2 they give the part number.

fields.name: REV
fields.text: Gives the revision of the device.

registers.name: WDTCON
registers.title: WATCHDOG TIMER CONTROL REGISTER

fields.name: REGSLP
fields.text: Sets whether the voltage regulator drops to Low-Power mode when the device sleeps; disabled on PIC18LF devices.

values.text: Regulator in Low-Power mode during Sleep.
Regulator stays in normal mode during Sleep.

fields.name: ULPLVL
fields.text: Output of the Ultra Low-Power Wake-up comparator, reporting the RA0 voltage against about 0.5 V; meaningful only with ULPEN = 1.

fields.name: SRETEN
fields.text: Lets the device enter Ultra Low-Power mode in Sleep; available only when RETEN# (CONFIG1L<0>) = 0.

values.text: With RETEN# = 0 and the regulator on, Sleep puts the device in Ultra Low-Power mode.
Regulator on in Sleep; REGSLP governs its Low-Power mode.

fields.name: ULPEN
fields.text: Turns the Ultra Low-Power Wake-up module on or off.

values.text: Module on; ULPLVL shows its comparator output.

fields.name: ULPSINK
fields.text: Turns on the Ultra Low-Power Wake-up current sink; meaningful only with ULPEN = 1.

fields.name: SWDTEN
fields.text: Turns the Watchdog Timer on or off from software; no effect when WDTEN<1:0> enables the WDT.
